description: We are university students passionate about engineering, programming, technology, and innovation. For NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, we aim to develop an interactive Space Mission Design Game combining engineering, simulation, and game development. We welcome enthusiastic members interested in Python, C/C++, web development, game development, UI/UX, 3D modelling, and data analysis. Let's collaborate, innovate, and create something impactful!
summary: Space Max is an interactive, browser-based aerospace simulator and tycoon game designed to bridge the gap between abstract textbook equations and intuitive STEM education. Developed as a lightweight yet mathematically rigorous educational tool, the platform empowers students to explore orbital mechanics through a hands-on, failure-driven learning loop. Players engineer multi-stage rockets and pilot them using real-world physics paradigms. The simulation engine calculates true Newtonian forces frame-by-frame, requiring users to manage critical flight parameters such as Thrust-to-Weight Ratios (TWR), the Tsiolkovsky Rocket Equation for Delta-V optimization, and dynamic aerodynamic stress. During launch sequences, players must actively throttle down to mitigate structural failure during Max-Q and maintain precise pitch trajectories (e.g., 45° to 72°) to minimize gravity drag. By replacing vague "Game Over" screens with actionable telemetry diagnostics—detailing exact deviations in trajectory or aerodynamic stress—Space Max transforms failure into discovery. Inspired by authentic NASA mission profiles, from low Earth orbit deployments to complex interplanetary transits, Space Max gamifies rocket science to inspire the next generation of engineers.
